1.1.1:
Analyze compliance with WCAG SC 1.1.1 (Non-text Content).
Test rules:
1. Image buttons must have a non-empty accessible name.
2. Images must have non-empty accessible names unless decorative (alt="", role="presentation", aria-hidden="true").
3. Accessible names must be meaningful, not just filenames or "image".
4. Object elements must have accessible names.
5. SVG elements with explicit roles must have accessible names.
6. Text alternatives must serve the equivalent purpose of the non-text content in its context (the text shown in an image of text, the key facts of a chart, the destination or action of an image inside a link or button).
7. Images hidden from assistive technology (empty alt, role="presentation"/"none", aria-hidden, CSS background images) must not withhold information or functionality unavailable through accessible content.
8. Video and audio must have a text alternative that at least provides descriptive identification of the content.
9. Characters used as pictures — look-alike letters from other scripts, ASCII art, emoticons — must have a text alternative.
1.4.1:
Analyze compliance with WCAG SC 1.4.1 (Use of Color).
Test rules:
1. Links distinguished only by color must also have another visual indicator (underline, bold, different lightness, etc.).
2. Required or error form fields identified only by color must have an additional non-color indicator (asterisk, label text, icon, etc.).
3. The selected, current or active item among peers (tabs, navigation, pagination, filter chips, segmented buttons) must be marked by more than color.
4. Charts, maps, diagrams and status icons must not convey information by color alone.
1.4.13:
Analyze compliance with WCAG SC 1.4.13 (Content on Hover or Focus).
Test rules:
1. Additional content that appears on pointer hover or keyboard focus must be dismissible without moving pointer hover or keyboard focus, unless it communicates an input error or does not obscure or replace other content.
2. If pointer hover can trigger the additional content, the pointer must be able to move over that content without it disappearing.
3. The additional content must remain visible until the hover or focus trigger is removed, the user dismisses it, or its information is no longer valid.
2.1.1:
Analyze compliance with WCAG SC 2.1.1 (Keyboard).
Test rules:
1. Every control that can be operated with a pointer must be reachable with the keyboard and operable with Enter, Space or the keys its role implies.
2. A control must not remove keyboard focus from itself when it receives it.
3. Content and controls that appear on pointer hover must also be reachable with the keyboard.
4. Scrollable regions must be reachable with sequential keyboard navigation, and iframes containing visible, sequentially focusable functionality must not be removed from the Tab order.
5. Keyboard operation must not require specific timings for individual keystrokes.
2.1.2:
Analyze compliance with WCAG SC 2.1.2 (No Keyboard Trap).
Test rules:
1. If keyboard focus can be moved to a component, focus must be able to be moved away from it using only the keyboard.
2. If moving focus away requires more than unmodified arrow or Tab keys or other standard exit methods, the user must be advised of the method, and the method must work.
2.4.3:
Analyze compliance with WCAG SC 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
Test rules:
1. Focusable elements must receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability (positive tabindex, CSS reordering, and DOM order that differs from the visual order are the usual causes).
2. Content opened by a control (menu, dialog, disclosure) must come next in the focus order, and a modal dialog must keep focus inside while open.
2.4.4:
Analyze compliance with WCAG SC 2.4.4 (Link Purpose (In Context)).
A link passes if its purpose is clear from its accessible name OR from its surrounding context (same sentence, paragraph, list item, or table cell).
Test rules:
1. The link must have a non-empty accessible name.
2. The link in context must be descriptive (not just "click here", "read more", etc. unless context clarifies the destination).
3. Links with identical names in the same context must serve an equivalent purpose.
4. Elements that act as links (activating them navigates) without being marked up as links must also have a purpose that can be determined from their text or context.
2.4.7:
Analyze compliance with WCAG SC 2.4.7 (Focus Visible).
Test rules:
1. Every element that can receive keyboard focus must show a visible focus indicator when focused.
2. Focus moving within a composite widget (menu, listbox, grid, tab list, tree) must be visible.
3.3.1:
Analyze compliance with WCAG SC 3.3.1 (Error Identification).
Test rules:
1. If an input error is automatically detected, the item in error must be identified and the error described to the user in text.
4.1.3:
Analyze compliance with WCAG SC 4.1.3 (Status Messages).
Test rules:
1. Status messages must be programmatically determinable through role or properties, so assistive technology can present them without the message receiving focus.
2. The live region must exist before the status message is inserted into it.
3. A status conveyed by an image, icon or colour change must have a text alternative that is presented as a status message.
